text.en:
Asha dropped a steel pin in a heap of sand. She could not see it.
Her grandfather brought a small bar magnet and moved it over the sand.
The pin jumped up and stuck to the magnet! Asha laughed. "The magnet found it for me!"

A magnet attracts some things. Things that a magnet attracts are called magnetic. Iron, steel, nickel and cobalt are magnetic.
Things that a magnet does not attract are non-magnetic. Plastic, wood, paper, glass, rubber and copper are non-magnetic.
Every magnet has two ends called poles: the north pole and the south pole. The pull is strongest at the poles.
Unlike poles attract each other (north and south). Like poles repel each other (north and north, or south and south).
A freely hanging bar magnet turns and rests in the north-south direction. A compass works in this way.
A magnet pulls some things towards it. We say it attracts them. Iron and steel are attracted.
Plastic, wood, paper and glass are not attracted. They are non-magnetic.
A magnet has two poles, north and south. Unlike poles attract and like poles push each other away.
A bar magnet hanging freely always settles along the north-south direction.

problem.en: Ravi has a nail, a coin made of copper, a rubber and a steel spoon. Which ones will a magnet attract?

text.en: Check what each thing is made of: iron, copper, rubber, steel.

why.en: The material decides if it is magnetic.

text.en: Iron and steel are magnetic. Copper and rubber are not.

why.en: Only iron, steel, nickel and cobalt are attracted.

text.en: So the magnet attracts the nail and the steel spoon.

why.en: The nail is iron and the spoon is steel.

prompt.en: A friend says every metal sticks to a magnet. Explain why she is not right.

requiredIdeas.en: Only some metals such as iron, steel, nickel and cobalt are magnetic.
Metals such as copper, aluminium and gold are not attracted by a magnet.

points.en: Magnets attract iron, steel, nickel and cobalt.
Plastic, wood, paper, glass and copper are non-magnetic.
Unlike poles attract; like poles repel.
A hanging bar magnet rests in the north-south direction.
